claims.text: An earlier draft of this module hand-rolled worktree creation, commit, and patch capture for each concurrent write task. That was wrong: it duplicated ``daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt``, which already does exactly that
claims.why: Refers to code outside this chunk (TaskAttempt in spine.attempt). Cannot verify the claim without that code.

claims.text: ``TaskAttempt`` is independently tested to leave the primary checkout byte-identical (``tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_happy_path_artifact_and_primary_untouched``) and to expose NO apply/promote/land path (``tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_module_exposes_no_apply_path``).
claims.why: References test files not present in this chunk. Cannot verify test existence or results.

claims.text: Phase 1 -- CONCURRENT GATING (``gate_candidates``). Turn each write Assignment into a ``TaskSpec``, run it through ``TaskAttempt`` with ``offload()`` as the runner ... fanned out across a thread pool, every attempt in its own worktree.
claims.why: References functions (gate_candidates, offload) and classes (TaskSpec, TaskAttempt) not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``run_write_wave`` additionally asks Phase 1 to persist those bytes in the checkout-external Daedalus artifact archive.
claims.why: References run_write_wave and artifact archive not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Phase 2 -- PROMOTION (``promote_candidates``; opt-in, a separate call, NOT wired into ``KairosScheduler.dispatch()``'s default path
claims.why: References promote_candidates and KairosScheduler.dispatch not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: promotion is: * guarded by ONE cross-process lock (``_PromotionLock``, the same msvcrt/fcntl pattern as ``daedalus.budget._BudgetLock`` and ``runs/council/room.py``'s ``_RoomLock``, independently written here because both of those are private to modules this file does not own)
claims.why: References _PromotionLock, _BudgetLock, _RoomLock not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: applied into ONE dedicated "integration" worktree, one candidate at a time, NEVER into the primary checkout
claims.why: References integration worktree concept not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: cumulatively RE-GATED after every apply (the project's configured test command, re-run against the integration state via ``daedalus.spine.attempt.command_gate``
claims.why: References command_gate not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: for any candidate whose artifact was captured against a base the integration branch has since moved past ... RE-ATTEMPTED (a fresh ``TaskAttempt``, same objective, ``base_revision`` = the current integration HEAD) rather than force-applied stale.
claims.why: References re-attempt logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Phase 3 -- SEALED HANDOFF (``run_write_wave``). Earlier revisions allowed a per-repo setting to call ``promote_candidates`` automatically after gating. That still crossed the candidate -> integration boundary without an owner, even though primary merge remained manual. The adopted Iron Plan closes that path: a write wave may gate and persist candidates, but it always returns them held. ``promote_candidates`` remains a separate explicit owner operation.
claims.why: References run_write_wave and promote_candidates not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``Assignment.paths`` are collected from whatever the caller supplied to ``KairosScheduler`` -- ``kairos/decompose.py``'s own system prompt asks the local model for "repo-relative path", but other callers (the web API, an editor extension) hand through whatever the client sent, which can be an ABSOLUTE path into the PRIMARY checkout.
claims.why: References Assignment, KairosScheduler, and kairos/decompose.py not present in this chunk.

claims.text: That matters here because ``TaskSpec.target_paths`` is compared, verbatim, against ``PatchArtifact.changed_paths`` -- which are always repo-relative POSIX strings from ``git diff --name-only`` inside the WORKTREE (see ``daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._capture_patch``/the "escaped target_paths" check in ``_run_with_ledger``).
claims.why: References TaskSpec, PatchArtifact, _capture_patch, _run_with_ledger not defined in this chunk.
